title: Sensor magnet mounting device having an improved mounting structure

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.

claims.note: This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper for gripping a ferromagnetic workpiece.

claims.quote: a magnet housing containing a magnet therein
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnet within a housing, but does not disclose the magnet being displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping position and a release position, nor for gripping a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference does not disclose pole shoes attached to a housing, or workpiece contact surfaces designed to guide a magnetic field portion.
This reference does not disclose a workpiece contact surface or a contact surface angle relative to a displacement direction.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper, and does not mention any contact surface angle or its range.
This reference describes a magnet mounting device and does not mention a housing extending along a longitudinal axis in the context of a magnetic gripper.
This reference describes a magnet mounting device and does not mention a displacement direction aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis of a housing.
This reference describes a magnet mounting device and does not mention pole shoes with an active structure for directing a magnetic field portion.
This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device for a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with an active structure having a bevel.
This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device for a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with a bevel and workpiece contact surface defining a bevel angle.
This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device for a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with a bevel angle ranging in size from 5° to 85°.

This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device for a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with an active structure having a plurality of projections for directing a magnetic field and forming a workpiece contact surface.

claims.quote: at least a pair of projecting members 3 each constituting a cylindrical portion projecting from said magnet housing
claims.note: The reference discloses at least a pair of projecting members, which can be interpreted as a first and second projection.

claims.quote: at least a pair of projecting members 3 each constituting a cylindrical portion projecting from said magnet housing, said projecting members being spaced to define a gap to receive said spoke
claims.note: The projecting members are spaced to define a gap, implying they are adjacent to one another.

claims.quote: said projecting members being spaced to define a gap to receive said spoke
claims.note: The gap between the projecting members functions as a recess.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a 'gap' between projecting members, not a 'recess' in an 'active structure'—different terminology and unclear structural relationship.

claims.note: The reference does not specify any dimensional relationship between the recess and the projections, particularly regarding a deviation of at most 25%.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet on a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with a positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a magnet mounting device and does not mention pole shoes, or a first and second pole shoe.
This reference describes a magnet mounting device and does not mention pole shoes, or north and south poles.
This reference describes a fixed magnet mounting device, not a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet.
This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device, not a magnetic gripper with a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device, not a magnetic gripper with a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a magnet housing, not a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or supply line.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet on a bicycle spoke, not a magnetic gripper with a manipulator interface.
The reference describes a magnet housing but does not mention any design features to suppress the escape of the magnetic field.
The reference describes a magnet housing but does not mention any shielding device to prevent the magnetic field from escaping.
The reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper system.
The reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper and a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper system with gripping and release states for a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper system with gripping and release states for a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a mounting device for a magnet, not a magnetic gripper system with projections and a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a magnet housing and projecting members, but not a receptacle in the form of a groove.

overall.why: This reference describes a sensor magnet mounting device for a bicycle spoke, which is entirely unrelated to a magnetic gripper with displaceable magnets and pole shoes for handling workpieces.
